keyPoints.en: Unicellular organisms (Amoeba) exchange gases by diffusion across the plasma membrane — large surface area to volume ratio.
keyPoints.bm: Organisma unisel (Amoeba) menukar gas secara resapan merentasi membran plasma — nisbah luas permukaan kepada isi padu besar.

keyPoints.en: Insects: tracheal system — spiracles, tracheae (with chitin rings), tracheoles reaching every cell.
keyPoints.bm: Serangga: sistem trakea — spirakel, trakea (dengan gelang kitin), trakeol yang sampai ke setiap sel.

keyPoints.en: Fish: gills with filaments and lamellae; water flows opposite to blood (countercurrent) for maximum O₂ uptake.
keyPoints.bm: Ikan: insang dengan filamen dan lamela; air mengalir bertentangan dengan darah (arus lawan) untuk pengambilan O₂ maksimum.

keyPoints.en: Amphibians: moist skin and simple lungs. Humans: lungs with millions of alveoli.
keyPoints.bm: Amfibia: kulit lembap dan peparu ringkas. Manusia: peparu dengan berjuta-juta alveolus.

question.en: Why do large organisms need special respiratory structures?
question.bm: Mengapa organisma besar memerlukan struktur respirasi khas?

answer.en: Their surface area to volume ratio is small, so diffusion through the skin alone can't supply enough O₂.
answer.bm: Nisbah luas permukaan kepada isi padu kecil, jadi resapan melalui kulit sahaja tidak cukup membekalkan O₂.

tip.en: For each organism: name the structure + one adaptation for efficient gas exchange.
tip.bm: Bagi setiap organisma: namakan struktur + satu penyesuaian untuk pertukaran gas yang cekap.

keyPoints.en: Air pathway: nostrils → nasal cavity → pharynx → larynx → trachea → bronchi → bronchioles → alveoli.
keyPoints.bm: Laluan udara: lubang hidung → rongga hidung → farinks → larinks → trakea → bronkus → bronkiol → alveolus.

keyPoints.en: Inhalation: external intercostals and diaphragm contract; ribs move up/out; diaphragm flattens; volume ↑, pressure ↓, air in.
keyPoints.bm: Tarikan nafas: interkosta luar dan diafragma mengecut; rusuk naik/keluar; diafragma mendatar; isi padu ↑, tekanan ↓, udara masuk.

keyPoints.en: Exhalation: muscles relax; ribs move down/in; diaphragm domes up; volume ↓, pressure ↑, air out.
keyPoints.bm: Hembusan nafas: otot mengendur; rusuk turun/masuk; diafragma melengkung ke atas; isi padu ↓, tekanan ↑, udara keluar.

keyPoints.en: Frogs use the buccopharyngeal floor to pump air into their lungs (positive pressure).
keyPoints.bm: Katak menggunakan lantai bukofarinks untuk mengepam udara ke dalam peparu (tekanan positif).

question.en: In the bell-jar model, what do the rubber sheet and balloons represent?
question.bm: Dalam model balang loceng, apakah yang diwakili oleh kepingan getah dan belon?

answer.en: Rubber sheet = diaphragm; balloons = lungs; jar = thoracic cavity.
answer.bm: Kepingan getah = diafragma; belon = peparu; balang = rongga toraks.

tip.en: Volume and pressure always change in OPPOSITE directions (Boyle's law!).
tip.bm: Isi padu dan tekanan sentiasa berubah dalam arah BERTENTANGAN (hukum Boyle!).

keyPoints.en: Alveoli adaptations: wall one cell thick, moist lining, very large total surface area, dense capillary network.
keyPoints.bm: Penyesuaian alveolus: dinding setebal satu sel, lapisan lembap, jumlah luas permukaan sangat besar, rangkaian kapilari padat.

keyPoints.en: O₂ diffuses from alveolar air (high concentration) into blood; CO₂ diffuses from blood into alveoli.
keyPoints.bm: O₂ meresap dari udara alveolus (kepekatan tinggi) ke dalam darah; CO₂ meresap dari darah ke alveolus.

keyPoints.en: O₂ is carried as oxyhaemoglobin; it is released in tissues where O₂ concentration is low.
keyPoints.bm: O₂ diangkut sebagai oksihemoglobin; ia dibebaskan di tisu yang berkepekatan O₂ rendah.

keyPoints.en: CO₂ is carried mainly as HCO₃⁻ ions in plasma.
keyPoints.bm: CO₂ diangkut terutamanya sebagai ion HCO₃⁻ dalam plasma.

keyPoints.en: Breathing rate is controlled by the medulla oblongata, which detects CO₂ levels in the blood.
keyPoints.bm: Kadar pernafasan dikawal oleh medula oblongata yang mengesan aras CO₂ dalam darah.

question.en: Why does exhaled air contain more CO₂ than inhaled air?
question.bm: Mengapa udara hembusan mengandungi lebih CO₂ daripada udara tarikan?

answer.en: CO₂ from respiring cells diffuses from the blood into the alveoli and is breathed out.
answer.bm: CO₂ daripada sel yang berespirasi meresap dari darah ke alveolus dan dihembus keluar.

tip.en: Inhaled air ≈ 21% O₂, 0.04% CO₂. Exhaled ≈ 16% O₂, 4% CO₂.
tip.bm: Udara tarikan ≈ 21% O₂, 0.04% CO₂. Hembusan ≈ 16% O₂, 4% CO₂.

keyPoints.en: Insects: O₂ diffuses directly from tracheoles into cells — no blood needed to carry O₂.
keyPoints.bm: Serangga: O₂ meresap terus dari trakeol ke sel — tidak perlu darah untuk mengangkut O₂.

keyPoints.en: Fish: as water passes over the lamellae, O₂ diffuses into blood capillaries; countercurrent keeps a gradient along the whole gill.
keyPoints.bm: Ikan: apabila air melalui lamela, O₂ meresap ke kapilari darah; arus lawan mengekalkan kecerunan sepanjang insang.

keyPoints.en: Amphibians: gas exchange through moist, thin, highly vascularised skin, plus lungs.
keyPoints.bm: Amfibia: pertukaran gas melalui kulit lembap, nipis dan banyak salur darah, serta peparu.

keyPoints.en: Plants: gases diffuse through stomata (leaves) and lenticels (stems), then through air spaces.
keyPoints.bm: Tumbuhan: gas meresap melalui stoma (daun) dan lentisel (batang), kemudian melalui ruang udara.

question.en: Why must a frog's skin stay moist?
question.bm: Mengapa kulit katak mesti sentiasa lembap?

answer.en: Gases must dissolve in moisture before diffusing across the skin.
answer.bm: Gas mesti melarut dalam lembapan sebelum meresap merentasi kulit.

tip.en: Countercurrent flow = water and blood move in opposite directions.
tip.bm: Aliran arus lawan = air dan darah bergerak dalam arah bertentangan.

keyPoints.en: Asthma: airways narrow and swell (allergens, dust, haze) → wheezing; treated with inhalers.
keyPoints.bm: Asma: saluran udara menyempit dan membengkak (alergen, debu, jerebu) → berdehit; dirawat dengan inhaler.

keyPoints.en: Bronchitis: inflamed bronchi with excess mucus; emphysema: damaged alveolar walls, less surface area.
keyPoints.bm: Bronkitis: bronkus radang dengan mukus berlebihan; emfisema: dinding alveolus rosak, luas permukaan berkurang.

keyPoints.en: Lung cancer: mainly from tar in cigarette smoke; also asbestos and radon.
keyPoints.bm: Kanser peparu: terutamanya daripada tar dalam asap rokok; juga asbestos dan radon.

keyPoints.en: Smoke contains tar, nicotine, carbon monoxide and irritants that paralyse cilia.
keyPoints.bm: Asap mengandungi tar, nikotina, karbon monoksida dan perengsa yang melumpuhkan silia.

keyPoints.en: Prevention: no smoking or vaping, masks during haze, exercise, avoid polluted air.
keyPoints.bm: Pencegahan: tidak merokok atau vape, pakai topeng semasa jerebu, bersenam, elakkan udara tercemar.

question.en: Why do smokers often have a 'smoker's cough'?

answer.en: Damaged cilia can't sweep mucus away, so it builds up and must be coughed out.
answer.bm: Silia yang rosak tidak dapat menyapu mukus, jadi mukus terkumpul dan perlu dibatukkan keluar.

tip.en: Link each disease to the structure damaged and how gas exchange is affected.
tip.bm: Kaitkan setiap penyakit dengan struktur yang rosak dan kesannya terhadap pertukaran gas.
